data.completion_memo: P0, P1, P2.3 and P2.4 landed and pushed as three separate commits (53691c5, 2dc867f, ddbcf08), each verified green before the next. P0 removes the app-wide lockout class: nested hashes verified over stored bytes, durable records tolerate unknown keys, frozen-record reads scoped by chat id, compatibility tests plus an Adashi QA job. P1 makes the run path degrade instead of killing a message: shape/availability refusals become notices and dropped bindings, mid-Chat edits fall back to the frozen snapshot, Send gates on the selected/frozen workflow, the start-path panic is a typed refusal, validate-what-was-just-written is gone, and save surfaces the core verdict. P2.3 collapses the duplicate digest rules into one shared implementation with byte-identical output. P2.4 adds a frozen-record version gate: current validates, older goes through an explicit migration table, newer opens read-only with a notice instead of failing. REMAINING (deliberately not forced; weeks-scale per the spec): P2.1 one capability registry, P2.2 editor consumes structured verdicts and the TypeScript twin validator is removed, P2.5 redundant re-validation/compiled-pass caching, P2.6 path/rule/value diagnostics, and declaration-order sensitivity in command_fingerprint (blocked on a stored-record migration). Recorded in design doc aworkit.validate_freeze_hardening.implementation_record. Verification: cargo test --lib 595 passed / 1 pre-existing unrelated comfyui failure; pnpm check clean; vitest 622/623 with one flaky Settings timeout that passes 51/51 in isolation.

lines:
WHY THIS EXISTS

Three consecutive user-visible outages in two days came from one chain: a feature task added a new capability family (native ComfyUI tools) and five hand-written registries that classify tool ids were never told about it. The user's messages died with, in order:
1. "stored settings document is invalid: unknown field bridgeServerId" -> every command failed -> "Chat projection unavailable" (app unusable).
2. "workflow 'workflow.custom.3' is not executable: ... toolIds must reference tool.<name> or mcp:<server> bindings".
3. "stored frozen Chat tool bindings failed integrity validation".
4. Silent: the freeze path dropped both ComfyUI authoring helpers because a prefix test preceded the exact-id test.
None of these was a tampering event. Every one rejected an artifact this build itself wrote.

The design model already forbids the behaviour. aworkit.trusted_core.snapshot_freezer (continuation clarification, 2026-09-19) says: do not re-freeze tool metadata and then reject the Chat because installed metadata differs; do not pin tool schema, description, provider name or limits to the Chat; each invocation records the interface it used as evidence, without enforcing it later; explicit adapter compatibility is checked at dispatch, never as an app-upgrade Chat-lockout gate. aworkit.workflow_worker.failure_policy adds: dispatch must degrade, because a rejected dispatch is a dead run. The implementation turned an evidence record into an enforcement gate.

READ FIRST (in this order)
1. The design specification linked to this task, aworkit.validate_freeze_hardening ("Validation and freeze: why it keeps breaking, and the ordered fix"). It carries the measured surface, the verified traps, the two-hash-rule analysis, the ranked time bombs, the target design and the phase plan. Retrieve it in full with adashi_design get_documents (ids: ["markdown:aworkit.validate_freeze_hardening"]).
2. aworkit.workflow_worker.failure_policy and the snapshot_freezer element description (they are normative).
3. The code anchors named below. Verify every line reference before relying on it; the tree changes.

MEASURED BASELINE (do not re-derive, but do re-verify the numbers you depend on)
- The selected workflow document is fully validated 3x per start (service.rs:1962 freeze, pipeline.rs:3489 worker request validation, pipeline.rs:2433 dispatch compile) and 2x per follow-up; the 128 KiB bound is recomputed 3x per start; validate_v1_executable_catalog alone has 71 distinct error sites across ~15 helpers in documents.rs:1436-2345.
- A frozen record is re-validated once at write (history.rs:806) and then ~2N-3N times per command on a profile with N past Chats (history.rs:629, :649, :686, :699, :1449 each decode all or until-match).
- Tool settings are frozen 2-3x per action in two different representations: service-layer FrozenToolBindingV1 (workflow_tools.rs:10, current_configuration.rs:95) and worker-layer StoredFileToolBindingV1 (tool_loop.rs:1204, twice per fresh start).
- 184 refusal sites in the four modules on the path; ~46 groups of user-visible refusal messages.
- The workflow schema is enforced twice, independently: ~1000 lines of Rust vs the 813-line desktop/src/workbench/workflowExecution.ts (~45 rules), with 5 Rust<->TS drift pairs.
- 34 Rust + 13 TypeScript capability-family vocabulary sites.
- No QA job covers "a profile written by the previous build still opens its Chats".
- Current suite baseline: cargo test --lib = 564 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.

SCOPE

P0 - REMOVE THE OUTAGE CLASS (do this first, alone, and verify it)
P0.1 Verify nested snapshot hashes from stored bytes. history.rs:1925 validate_frozen_context_record recomputes model_tier_hash/provider_hash/model_hash (:1957-:1959), tool_hash (:2059) and, in project_scope.rs:124-125, the project and workspace hashes from TODAY'S decoded structs. Any field added to ProviderConfigurationV2, ModelConfigurationV2, ModelTierConfigurationV2 (or a variant field), BuiltInToolConfigurationV2, ProjectConfigurationV2 or WorkspaceConfigurationV2 that serializes at its default invalidates every stored Chat. The context's own hash already does this correctly: history.rs:1866-1877 hashes the raw stored value["context"] and compares it (Rule A). Apply Rule A to every nested snapshot: thread the stored record Value into the validator and compare each stored hash against the canonical hash of its stored JSON sub-value. Keep the write path (history.rs:801-806) hashing the struct it just built. Tamper detection must remain byte-exact.
P0.2 Durable records tolerate unknown keys instead of failing. deny_unknown_fields is set on the durable record types at history.rs:80,87,95,122,189,197,213; settings_v2.rs:936 (BuiltInToolConfigurationV2); tool_registry.rs:24 (ToolOptions); dto.rs:12 (UiCommandInput). Removing a field currently makes every previously written record undecodable - that is exactly the bridgeServerId outage. Make durable decoding tolerant (drop unknown keys, report a notice) while keeping typo detection where a human edits: note BuiltInToolConfigurationV2 is shared between Settings and frozen snapshots, so if you drop the serde attribute, add an explicit unknown-key check in the Settings validation path (settings_v2.rs) so editor strictness is preserved.
P0.3 Read only what the command needs. Stop decoding and validating every stored record on every command. The profile-level aggregate scan is why ONE bad record breaks every Chat, breaks starting a new Chat (freeze_context re-reads all contexts at history.rs:807) and can break app open (ensure_history_summaries -> frozen_contexts at history.rs:877-887). Introduce a chat-id index or filter by chat id BEFORE decoding, and keep the exhaustive scan only in the explicit diagnostics/repair path.
P0.4 Add the compatibility QA job (see VERIFICATION). This is the safety net whose absence let all three regressions ship.
P0 exit criteria: cargo test --lib green; a profile with one deliberately unreadable unrelated record still opens, lists Chats and starts a new Chat; a stored record with an extra unknown key in a nested snapshot, and one missing a newly added field, both still load and keep their hash verification; a tampered stored value is still rejected; the new QA job passes and demonstrably fails on the pre-P0 code.

P1 - MAKE VALIDATION INCAPABLE OF KILLING A MESSAGE
P1.1 Apply the failure policy to the freeze/validate chain. The precedent already exists in this codebase: per-tool-call argument validation degrades into a model-visible tool error ("Frozen argument validation is the recoverable execution boundary", tool_loop.rs:3449-3451). Convert shape and availability refusals on the run path into committed notices and dropped bindings, as freeze_graph_bindings already does for unavailable tools (workflow_tools.rs:53,65,148,182). Reserve hard failure for the three conditions the policy permits. Do not introduce any new terminating condition.
P1.2 Fall back to the frozen snapshot. current_configuration.rs:36-68 prefers a live library entry and uses the frozen snapshot only when the entry no longer resolves, so editing a saved workflow mid-Chat into a non-executable state blocks every later message of a running Chat. Fall back to the frozen snapshot with a notice.
P1.3 Send must depend on the selected workflow, not the library default. service.rs:576-580 validates the default workflow; :555 stores the failure as disabled_reason; desktop/src/chat/composer.ts:44 turns it into a disabled Send button.
P1.4 Remove the start-path panic. service.rs:1995 .expect("at least one model tier is resolved") is reachable; make it a typed refusal that names the fix.
P1.5 Stop validating what was just written. history.rs:806 validates the record it just built; service.rs:1280-1284 compares the persisted record to the one just passed (structurally dead).
P1.6 Reconcile save with execute. documents.rs:346,357 lets a document be saved that the catalog will refuse at start (the editor deliberately preserves unknown node types - WorkflowPropertiesPane.tsx:236), and the refusal names one of 71 rules the user never saw. Preservation on save is a design invariant, so keep saving, but surface the core verdict (structured: path, rule, value) at save time and on open, and make the start refusal name the fix.
P1 exit criteria: a mid-Chat edit no longer blocks a running Chat; an unrelated broken default workflow does not disable Send; a stored-binding shape mismatch degrades to a notice instead of failing the message; no panic; all with tests.

P2 - ONE SCHEMA, ONE REGISTRY, ONE HASH, VERSIONED RECORDS
P2.1 Capability registry. Define one family abstraction providing matches(id), descriptor(id, settings), frozen_configuration(...), validate_frozen_shape(configuration) and dispatch(...); implement it for built-in, MCP selection, MCP function, ComfyUI workflow tool, ComfyUI authoring helper and delegation/subagent; then delete the prefix tests and fixed id sets at the 34 Rust sites (the inventory lists them; the ranked top 5 are tool_loop.rs:1218/' :1498, history.rs:1888, pipeline.rs:1297 with continuation.rs:168, documents.rs:1649, tool_loop.rs:1797). Adding a family must become one implementation plus its tests.
P2.2 One schema verdict. validate_v1_executable_catalog stays the single authority; the editor consumes structured verdicts from a core command instead of re-implementing ~45 rules in workflowExecution.ts; delete the TS twin, the 5 drift pairs and the now-stale TS messages.
P2.3 One digest rule. Four digest rules share the sha256: prefix today: three duplicate canonical_hash copies (history.rs:2152, pipeline.rs:3699, tool_loop.rs:5348), command_fingerprint (service.rs:4613, field-declaration-order sensitive, feeds start_command_hash inside the JCS-hashed context) and approvals::digest (approvals.rs:160, key-order tolerant only because preserve_order happens not to be enabled on a normal dependency edge). Collapse to one rule, remove declaration-order sensitivity, and make approvals::digest explicitly order-independent.
P2.4 Version gate and migration for frozen records. schema_version is asserted, never used to select rules, and there is no migrate function for frozen records (Settings has one: documents.rs:657-713). Unknown newer version becomes read-only with a notice, never an unrunnable Chat. The event's outer schemaVersion is checked only at write time (aworkit-local-store ledger payload_schema) and ignored on read.
P2.5 Delete redundant re-validation and the O(N) scan. One catalog validation at freeze plus byte-exact hash verification afterwards; drop the duplicate validation inside compile_graph_pass for an already-validated frozen snapshot and cache the compiled pass by snapshot hash; stop recomputing the 128 KiB bound three times per start.
P2.6 Diagnostics that name the thing. Every refusal reports {path, rule, value}. The ~19 bare "stored ... failed integrity validation" / "is not executable" strings must say which field, which rule and which value.
P2 exit criteria: a test registers a synthetic new capability family and shows it flowing through catalog -> freeze -> stored record -> admission -> dispatch without touching any other site; editor and Rust suites green; the compatibility QA job still passes; the O(N) per-command record scan is gone.

CONSTRAINTS AND NON-GOALS
- Keep these invariants: unknown workflow nodes and configuration fields are preserved losslessly; missing or incompatible capabilities never stop preparation, inspection, editing, execution or export; committed evidence is never rewritten or replayed; authority and approval decisions remain the broker's, and capability-host admission plus manifest version/hash checks stay hard-failing (that is a real trust boundary).
- Do not weaken tamper evidence: after P0.1 a tampered stored value must still be rejected byte-exactly, with a test proving it.
- Prefer conformance to the design model over new mechanisms. If a change contradicts aworkit.trusted_core.snapshot_freezer or aworkit.workflow_worker.failure_policy, the code is wrong; if you believe the design is wrong, record that in design and raise it instead of silently diverging.
- No release versions or installer bundles for testing (project rule). Use debug builds and a copied profile.
- Land P0 as its own commit/review before P1, and P1 before P2, so each phase is independently verifiable and revertible.

VERIFICATION RECIPE (this is what actually caught the real failures)
- Build a probe that opens a COPY of the user's real profile (copy %APPDATA%\\com.aworkit.desktop to a scratch directory; never open the live one) via DesktopRuntime::open(<copy>\\runtime) and iterates every stored frozen context, asserting each validates. A temporary in-crate test guarded by an environment variable works and must be removed afterwards. The live profile has 116 stored frozen Chats; all must validate.
- Negative control: revert each fix and confirm the exact user-visible message reappears. Do not claim a fix without reproducing the failure first.
- cargo test --lib (baseline 564 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored) and, for editor changes, the desktop vitest suites.
- cargo fmt --check on changed files only: the repo is not rustfmt-clean globally, so do not reformat unrelated files.
- Compatibility QA job: add an Adashi QA job (adashi_qa) that opens a checked-in fixture profile whose frozen records were written by the previous schema and asserts every Chat resolves a projection and one stub-provider turn completes, plus the two tolerance cases (extra unknown key, missing newly added field) and one tamper case. It must fail on the pre-P0 code.

DEFINITION OF DONE
P0, P1 and P2 implemented, each verified by tests that failed before the change; the compatibility QA job created and green; the design document aworkit.validate_freeze_hardening updated (or superseded by a new decision document) to record what actually changed, including any deviation from the plan and why; task finished with a lean completion memo pointing at the evidence.

data.title: Refactor the validate/freeze chain: hash stored bytes, one capability registry, one schema verdict, versioned records (P0 -> P1 -> P2)
